payload.name: Ordinal-work-questions-match-by-order
payload.description: When a question asks about the nth work in a person's series (e.g., third screenplay, second album), retrieve all candidate works and identify the nth by explicit ordinal or by chronological order before answering.
content: If the question uses an ordinal (first, second, third...) with a work category (screenplay, book, album, film), treat it as asking for the nth item in that person's chronological series of such works.

Do not answer from the first memory that mentions the category. Retrieve multiple candidate works (including completion/achievement events) and compare explicit ordinal labels or world_start dates to determine the true nth item.

If the candidate memories do not establish order, run an additional search for the person's completed works or a paraphrase of the work's theme before answering; never assume a title refers to the requested ordinal without evidence.

solves: The failure mechanism is treating the first memory that mentions the requested work category as sufficient evidence for an ordinal question, without verifying which item in the series it is. This applies to future questions asking about the nth creative work of a person (e.g., third screenplay, second novel, first album) when multiple works of that type exist and the ordering is not explicitly stated in a single memory. It must not apply to questions that name a specific work directly (e.g., 'What is Finding Home about?') or when only one work of that type exists.
